transcript.text: I sell roofing and exterior remodeling.
We do close to $6 million this year and
I'd like to be at $100 million.
What's stopping me and I'll be a little
vulnerable is the fear of losing family
time. Is there a path where I can work
no more than I currently am?
>> Well, first off, I think you've actually
already achieved a level of success in
the business that it's actually
attainable because you already have
money. And so, if you have any amount of
margin, which I'm guessing you do, you
can take that margin into consistently
buy time back and work as little or as
much as you want. Now, your ability to
get to 100 billion is going to be
predicated on your skill in picking good
people from a hiring perspective and
leading those people so that you can get
the most out of them. And in fact, like
beyond a certain point, the money you
get it almost has nothing to do with the
time that you're putting into it and
really about the preferences that you
have around work. I mean, I know people
who make tons of money and spend very
little time working and I know tons of
people who make tons of money and spend
a lot of time working. It's more common
in the beginning of your career that you
have to basically sacrifice a lot of
time because you don't have the capital
and you have to do it because you have
to make up for the fact that no one else
is there and you have to go make the
money yourself and you have to do all
the work, right? But at a certain point,
there's enough leverage in the business
that you can do it. So, I think that
what you really need is
how do I attract and recruit somebody
who has the ability to lead my business
as well or better than me or the thing
that takes the most of my time even if
it's not leading the whole business,
maybe a department or division so that I
can just keep working the same amount
that I am. But I in no way see this as a
zero-sum game. You do not have to
sacrifice your family for your goals.
You just might have potentially
different timelines and the willingness
to lose money on wrong bets.
